title: Local purity of branch locus for a quasi-finite morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $x\in X$, and put $y=f(x)$. Suppose that $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], that $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], and that $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Suppose also that
$$\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}\geq1,$$
where dimension means Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every point $x'\in X$ such that $x$ belongs to the closure of $\{x'\}$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x'}=1$, assume that $f$ is unramified at $x'$ [def-weil-unramified-morphism], meaning that it restricts to an unramified morphism on some open neighbourhood of $x'$. Then $f$ is etale at $x$: it restricts to an etale morphism on some open neighbourhood of $x$ [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BMB, pione-lemma-purity (Purity of branch locus), statement, lines 5117–5164. This node cites the Stacks statement and proof, not the historical references in its reference environment.

proof.text: The common local dimension $d$ is a finite integer by the Noetherian local dimension theorem. Prove the assertion for all morphisms in the statement by strong induction on $d\geq1$. Restrict to affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $y$ on which $f$ is of finite type, as supplied by quasi-finiteness at $x$. An open containing $x$ contains every generalization of $x$, with the same stalks, so the normality, dimension and codimension-one assumptions persist. In this restricted situation $x$ is isolated in its fibre.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, induction and local reduction; Algebra Tag 00KQ and Morphisms Tag 01TH.

proof.text: Apply the isolated-fibre-point finite-neighbourhood theorem. It supplies an etale map $b:U\to Y$, $u\mapsto y$, and an open $V\subset X\times_YU$ for which $g:V\to U$ is finite, has precisely one point $v$ over $u$, and sends $v$ to $x$. The projection $a:V\to X$ is etale: it is an open immersion followed by a base change of $b$. Shrink $U$ to an affine neighbourhood of $u$ and restrict $V$ to its inverse image; finiteness and the singleton fibre persist. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}S$, with primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ representing $u,v$. The rings can be chosen Noetherian: $U$ is locally of finite type over the locally Noetherian $Y$, and the finite $R$-algebra $S$ is Noetherian.

Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $B=S_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{V,v}$. The singleton-fibre stalk theorem makes $A\to B$ finite. Etale stalk invariance for $b$ and $a$ shows that $A$ is regular local, $B$ is a normal domain and $\dim A=\dim B=d$. In particular both rings are Noetherian: $A$ is regular local and $B$ is finite over $A$. To identify the local-base-change scheme explicitly, set $C=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}S$. Every maximal ideal of the finite $A$-algebra $C$ contracts to $\mathfrak pA$; the prime correspondence and the singleton fibre therefore give exactly one maximal ideal. Thus $C$ is local and its map to $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is an isomorphism: elements of $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ are already units in $C$. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}B=V\times_U\operatorname{Spec}A$, and its stalks are the corresponding stalks of $V$, by iterated localization.

source.place: Tag 05B8, lemma-finite-morphism-single-point-in-fibre, and its localization proof; More on Algebra Tags 07QP, 0AH0; Algebra Tags 033C, 033G, 00E3.

proof.text: Let $z$ be a height-one prime of $B$ and let $w\in V$ be its image. The localization identifications give $\dim\mathcal O_{V,w}=\dim B_z=1$, and $w$ generalizes $v$. Since $a$ is etale, stalk dimension invariance gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X,a(w)}=1$; continuity makes $a(w)$ a generalization of $x$. The hypothesis makes $f$ unramified at $a(w)$. The base-change formula for the unramified locus, first for $X\times_YU\to U$ and then for $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$, gives unramifiedness of $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ at $z$. Restriction to the open $V$ simply restricts the same unramified neighbourhoods. Thus $h$ has the required codimension-one assumption at every height-one prime of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, etale-local reduction; Morphisms Tag 0475, lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified.

proof.text: It suffices to prove that $h$ is etale. Here is the precise passage back to $g$ at $v$. Both $S/R$ and $B/A$ are finite, hence finitely presented algebras over their Noetherian base rings. If $h$ is etale, the etale-at-a-prime criterion applied to $A\to B$ at its maximal ideal gives flatness of $B$ over $A$ and $\Omega_{B/A}=0$. Localization of differentials identifies $(\Omega_{S/R})_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\Omega_{B/R}$. Every $R$-derivation $D$ of $B$ kills $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$: $D(r/t)=D(r)t^{-1}-rt^{-2}D(t)=0$. The universal property therefore identifies $\Omega_{B/R}$ with $\Omega_{B/A}$. Apply the same etale-at-a-prime criterion to $R\to S$ at $\mathfrak q$: its flatness hypothesis is exactly flatness over $R_{\mathfrak p}=A$. It gives an open neighbourhood $N$ of $v$ in $V$ on which $g$ is etale.

source.place: Tags 00FP, 00RT, 00U6 and 08WD; the elementary equality of R- and R_p-derivations supplies the target-localization identification.

proof.text: For such $N$, the composite $N\to U\to Y$ and the map $N\to X$ are etale. The image $O=a(N)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$, since etale morphisms are open. Factor $N\to X$ through $O$. This factor is etale by etale composition cancellation with the open immersion $O\to X$, and is surjective by the definition of $O$. Etale descent through this source cover shows that $f|_O$ is etale. Thus the local algebra conclusion promised in Step 5 proves the original assertion at $x$.

The finite map $A\to B$ is integral. Regular-local localization makes $A$ a regular ring; regular rings are normal, so its local ring $A$ is a normal domain. Let $P=\ker(A\to B)$, a prime because $B$ is a domain. The injection $A/P\hookrightarrow B$ is integral, so $\dim(A/P)=\dim B=d$. If $P\ne0$, a length-$d$ chain in $A/P$ lifts to a chain in $A$ starting at a prime containing $P$; prepending $(0)$ gives length at least $d+1$, a contradiction. Hence $A\hookrightarrow B$ is injective. Consequently $B$ is torsion free over $A$: a product of two nonzero elements in the domain $B$ cannot vanish.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, finite local injection; Algebra Tags 00GK, 0AFS, 0567, 00OK. The kernel dimension argument is written out.

proof.text: If $d=1$, the maximal ideal of $B$ is itself a height-one prime, so Step 4 makes $h$ unramified there. A regular local ring of dimension one is a DVR, hence a PID; the torsion-free module $B$ is therefore flat over $A$. Module finiteness gives finite algebra generation and hence finite presentation over the Noetherian $A$. Unramifiedness at the maximal ideal gives $\Omega_{B/A}=0$: on an affine unramified neighbourhood the differentials vanish, and their localization at the maximal ideal of the local ring $B$ is the module itself. The flat-and-unramified etale-at-a-prime criterion now gives an etale neighbourhood of this closed point. Any open neighbourhood of the closed point of a local spectrum is the whole spectrum. Thus $h$ is etale, proving the induction base.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, d=1; Algebra Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), More on Algebra Tag 0AUW, Algebra Tag 08WD.

proof.text: Suppose $d\geq2$. For every prime $Q\subset B$ with contraction $P\subset A$, one has $\dim B_Q=\dim A_P$. Indeed, incomparability contracts a strict prime chain ending at $Q$ to a strict chain ending at $P$. Conversely, going down for the integral extension of the normal domain $A$ lifts any chain ending at $P$ backwards, starting with the prescribed prime $Q$. Distinct contractions force distinct lifted primes. Taking suprema of chain lengths gives both height inequalities, and the localization dimension formula identifies heights with these local dimensions.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, going-down paragraph; Algebra Tags 00GT, 00H8, 00KF.

proof.text: Fix a nonzero prime $Q\ne\mathfrak m_B$ and put $P=Q\cap A$. The local ring $B_Q$ is normal, and $A_P$ is regular. The finite morphism $h$ is quasi-finite. Its two local dimensions are equal by Step 9, positive because $(0)\subsetneq Q$, and less than $d$: any chain below $Q$ can be extended by $\mathfrak m_B$. Every height-one generalization of $Q$ is a height-one prime of $B$ and is unramified by Step 4. These are precisely all the hypotheses of the induction assertion at $Q$, now at a strictly smaller positive dimension. Hence $h$ is etale at every such $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, induction at a nonclosed nongeneric point; Algebra Tags 00GY, 0AFS.

proof.text: The generic point needs no dimension-zero induction hypothesis. Choose a length-$d$ chain in the local domain $B$. A chain of maximal possible length starts at $(0)$ and ends at $\mathfrak m_B$, since otherwise it could be extended at an end. Its first nonzero prime $Q_1$ has height one: a longer chain below $Q_1$, followed by the remaining tail, would have length greater than $d$. Since $d\geq2$, $Q_1\ne\mathfrak m_B$, so Step 10 gives an etale open neighbourhood of $Q_1$. Every open containing $Q_1$ contains its generalization $(0)$. Thus $h$ is etale also at the generic point, and therefore at every point except possibly $\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 0BMB, lemma-purity, punctured-spectrum induction; explicit elementary treatment of the generic point left implicit in the source.

proof.text: Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $T^\circ=T\setminus\{\mathfrak m_A\}$. The inverse image $W^\circ$ is exactly $W\setminus\{\mathfrak m_B\}$: the map is local, and no proper subprime of $\mathfrak m_B$ has the same contraction, by incomparability. The restriction $W^\circ\to T^\circ$ is finite, and is etale by the open-cover locality of etaleness and Steps 10-11. Apply punctured-spectrum purity for the regular local ring $A$ of dimension at least two. It supplies a finite etale $E\to T$ and an isomorphism $W^\circ\simeq E\times_TT^\circ$ over $T^\circ$.

source.place: Tag 0BMA, lemma-local-purity, assertion (1), as invoked in the final paragraph of Tag 0BMB.

proof.text: The base $T$ is locally Noetherian and integral, with integrally closed stalks: $A$ is a normal domain and normality survives localization. Every stalk of $W$ is likewise a normal domain. The open $T^\circ$ is nonempty, since $d\geq2$; its inverse image in $W$ contains the generic point and is dense. Apply finite-normal dense-open comparison to the finite map $h:W\to T$, the finite etale map $E\to T$ from Step 12, and their specified isomorphism over $T^\circ$. It gives an isomorphism $W\simeq E$ over $T$. Therefore $h$ is etale. Steps 5-6 give an etale neighbourhood of the original $x$. This proves the inductive step and completes the strong induction.
